section2_card_paragraph.text: Every image on this page is an approved visualisation built to the general arrangement drawing for that exact size. The openings you count in a render are the openings on the drawing.

section2_card_bullets.text:
Six GA boards published, one for every approved size
Plan, four elevations, opening map and furniture schedule on one sheet
Door and window positions fixed before fabrication release
Full specification and all six drawings in one downloadable PDF

section2_card_cta_text.text: Ask us to check a drawing against your site

section2_card_image_alt.text: Indigo Grey 20 x 12 ft shipping container office, front long wall with window, door and window

variant_20x8_paragraph_1.text: The narrowest approved shell suits a gate office, a stores desk or a two-shift site cabin. Its general arrangement puts all three workstations on the rear long wall.

variant_20x8_paragraph_2.text: The front wall stays clear apart from the entrance, so nobody works with their back to the door. Six windows light the room: two on each long wall and one centred on each 8 ft end. At 8 ft wide the aisle is tight, so we keep both end walls free of furniture.

section3_20x8_bullets.text:
One 3 x 7 ft door and six 4 x 3 ft windows
Three workstations, all on the rear long wall
Front long wall carries the entrance and nothing else
One centred window on each 8 ft end wall
No partition, so the shell is one open room
Suits a gate post, a stores desk or a two-shift cabin

variant_20x10_paragraph_1.text: This is the reference size, and the rate card is anchored here at Rs 1,800 per sq ft. Two extra feet of width change the room completely. Now five people work in it: three along the rear wall and two either side of the door.

variant_20x10_paragraph_2.text: A clear aisle runs down the middle, so a chair can push back without blocking traffic. Most first-time buyers order this size, then scale up or down from its drawing. Six windows and one door keep the opening count identical to the 20 x 8 ft plan.

section3_20x10_bullets.text:
One door and six windows, the same count as the 20 x 8
Five workstations, three at the rear and two flanking the door
Clear central aisle runs the full twenty feet
Two feet wider than the 20 x 8 on the same length
The 200 sq ft reference the whole rate card is built from
Both end walls stay furniture-free for cross ventilation

variant_20x12_paragraph_1.text: The 12 ft shell is the 20 x 10 drawing widened by one foot on each long wall. Nothing else moves. The door keeps its position, the six windows keep theirs, and the desk count stays at five.

variant_20x12_paragraph_2.text: Every added inch becomes floor. Choose it when a survey table, a plan chest or a visitor chair must sit clear of the working aisle. Because the width grows and the seat count does not, the price per seat rises.

section3_20x12_bullets.text:
The 20 x 10 plan widened by one foot on each long wall
Five workstations, unchanged from the 20 x 10 drawing
One door and six windows, every position unchanged
The added width becomes circulation rather than seating
Room for a plan table or a visitor chair clear of the aisle

variant_30x10_paragraph_1.text: Thirty feet is where a site office becomes a team room. Twelve workstations line the two long walls, seven at the back and five at the front.

variant_30x10_paragraph_2.text: Two doors sit near the ends of the front wall, so a crew can enter one end while a meeting runs at the other. Eight windows keep the middle of a 30 ft box from going dark. The centre bay between the two window pairs stays solid, which is where we run services.

section3_30x10_bullets.text:
Two 3 x 7 ft doors, one near each end of the front wall
Eight windows: four rear, two front, one on each end wall
Twelve workstations, seven at the rear and five at the front
The front run is shorter because two doors take wall length
Solid centre bay between the window pairs carries the services
No partition, so the thirty feet stay one team room

variant_40x8_paragraph_1.text: The first ten feet at one end become a private manager cabin, and the remaining thirty stay open. A partition with a single 3 x 7 ft internal door separates them. The manager has no outside door of their own.

variant_40x8_paragraph_2.text: Visitors come through the common office, which is exactly how a site supervisor wants it. At 8 ft wide the common run carries seven desks on one wall only, and the front wall stays clear. Ten seats sit down in total once you count the manager and two visitors.

section3_40x8_bullets.text:
Ten feet at one end partitioned off as a manager cabin
Two external doors plus one 3 x 7 ft internal partition door
Ten windows spread across the forty foot length
Seven workstations, all on a single long wall
The manager has no separate outside door
Ten seats once the manager and two visitors are counted

variant_40x10_paragraph_1.text: The largest approved shell gives the manager a true 10 x 10 ft room with three outside windows. Behind the partition, twelve workstations fill the 30 ft common office, seven at the rear and five at the front.

variant_40x10_paragraph_2.text: Fifteen people can sit down at once, counting the manager and two visitor chairs. Two external doors serve the common office at either end. Order this size when one shell must hold a whole project team.

section3_40x10_bullets.text:
A square 10 x 10 ft manager room with three outside windows
Twelve workstations in the thirty foot common office
Two external doors, one at each end of the common office
Ten windows and one internal partition door
Fifteen seats including the manager and two visitor chairs
